name: Zoom-out picture trivia
summary: Each round starts on a tiny crop of a picture (an animal's eye, a texture, a corner of a landmark) that zooms out over a few seconds; tap the right answer before it's obvious, and early answers score more.
core_loop: see a tiny crop → it zooms out → tap a choice → whole picture shows → next round
rules: the picture starts several times magnified and zooms out by the clock
an answer shows the whole picture
points fall the longer you wait
a wrong answer or running out of time costs a life
scoring: points per right answer, plus a bonus for how zoomed in it still was
social_hooks: the same pictures for everyone that day, so a Group compares who named them earliest
challenge a friend to beat your early-guess bonus
content_needs: one picture per round, detailed all the way in (SVG frames today; generated_image or picture_pack for photos)
the answer and 3 near-miss choices per picture
example_prompts: Wildlife photography trivia: zoom in on a tiny crop of a photo and guess the animal before it zooms out
Extreme close-up quiz of kitchen objects
Zoomed in guess the Pokemon before it zooms out
Guess the bird from a close-up of its feathers
notes: authoring/games/zoom_safari.authoring.json is the worked example (SVG animals, passes the gate). Photos are generated (generated_image) or CC0 (picture_pack), never of people.

name: Cartoon quote guess
summary: A funny cartoon character (a generic caricature, never a real person's likeness) says a line in a speech bubble, often in another language or as half a saying; pick what it means or how it ends.
core_loop: see the cartoon and its line → pick the meaning or the ending → the reveal shows the answer with a reaction → next
rules: each round is one character and one line
the choices include believable wrong meanings
characters are invented caricatures, never a real person's face or name
social_hooks: share the funniest line with the Group
friends compare how many they got
content_needs: lines with their meanings and 3 wrong meanings (public-domain sayings or written by Muse)
one cartoon character per line (SVG or generated_image in a cartoon style)
difficulty_levers: how close the wrong meanings are
example_prompts: Guess what the French person is saying: quotes from funny famous French people with funny images of French people
Guess what the grumpy cartoon chef is saying in Italian
Funny cartoon grandmas say old sayings and I guess what they mean
notes: When a request names real or famous people, the plan says so plainly: the pictures are cartoon caricatures of invented characters (a beret-wearing baker, not a real person), and quotes are public-domain sayings or written for the game, not attributed to real people.
